definitions.explanation: A line composed of short dashes with gaps between them, used in diagrams, maps, technical drawings, and road markings. Contrasted with a solid line.

examples.japanese: {破線|はせん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{沿|そ}って→沿う：13279_sou⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧。
⟦{地図|ちず}→地図：02914_chizu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{破線|はせん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{登山道|とざんどう}→登山道：19132_tozandou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{表|あらわ}している→表す：01868_arawasu⟧。
examples.english: The dashed lines on the map indicate mountain trails.

examples.japanese: ⟦{設計図|せっけいず}→設計図：14805_sekkeizu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{見|み}えない→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦{部分|ぶぶん}→部分：03715_bubun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{破線|はせん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{表示|ひょうじ}する→表示する：26973_hyoujisuru⟧⟦{決|き}まり→決まり：02548_kimari⟧になっている。
examples.english: In technical drawings, it is conventional to show hidden parts with dashed lines.

notes:
A compound of {破|は} (broken) and ⟦{線|せん}→線：09901_sen⟧ (line). In technical drawing, {破線|はせん} specifically refers to lines made of short dashes, as distinct from ⟦{点線|てんせん}→点線：18308_tensen⟧ (dotted lines made of dots).

USAGE:
Used in technical drawing, engineering, cartography, graphic design, and everyday instructions (such as "cut here" lines on packaging). In technical drawing standards (JIS), {破線|はせん} specifically indicates hidden edges or outlines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {破線|はせん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧ — to indicate with a dashed line
- {破線|はせん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{沿|そ}って→沿う：13279_sou⟧ — along the dashed line
- {破線|はせん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧ — to enclose with a dashed line
- {一点鎖線|いってんさせん} — dash-dot line; another technical line type

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{実線|じっせん}→実線：20763_jissen⟧ — solid line; the contrasting continuous line
- ⟦{点線|てんせん}→点線：18308_tensen⟧ — dotted line; a line made of dots rather than dashes
- {二点鎖線|にてんさせん} — double-dot-dash line; used in technical drawings for centerlines
